description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—labeled in the legend as Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on the x-axis using a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 (1) to 10^3 (1000). The y-axis represents ACC (%) and spans from approximately 60% to 85%. The six methods are each represented by a distinct colored line with a unique marker: Base is black with circles, FT is blue with triangles, IKE is red with triangles, MEND is brown with diamonds, MEMIT is purple with diamonds, and ROME is green with squares. All lines show an upward trend as the co-occurrence number increases. At the start of the x-axis (co-occurrence number = 1), the Base method starts at approximately 63%, FT at 65%, IKE at 66%, MEND at 68%, MEMIT at 69%, and ROME at 75%. At the end of the x-axis (co-occurrence number = 1000), the Base method reaches approximately 77%, FT reaches 80%, IKE reaches 81%, MEND reaches 83%, MEMIT reaches 84%, and ROME reaches 85%. The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy across the entire range, while the Base method consistently achieves the lowest.
